presentingComplaint: Found unresponsive and cold at home by family; brought in with confusion and extreme lethargy over the preceding several days.
history: 74-year-old woman with known long-standing primary hypothyroidism (post-radioiodine ablation for Graves disease 15 years ago), reportedly poorly compliant with levothyroxine for the past several months after her prescription lapsed. Lives alone; family noticed progressive slowing of speech, increasing fatigue, constipation and cold intolerance over the past 3-4 weeks, culminating in worsening confusion over the last 2 days. No fever reported. Found this morning unarousable in an unheated house during a cold spell. No history of trauma, overdose, or alcohol use. No recent infection symptoms reported by family. Other history: hypertension on amlodipine.
examination: Obtunded, responds only to painful stimuli, GCS 8/15. Profoundly hypothermic and bradycardic. Dry, coarse, doughy skin with non-pitting periorbital and peripheral (myxoedematous) swelling. Macroglossia. Hoarse voice. Sparse lateral eyebrows. Delayed relaxation phase of ankle reflexes. Bradypnea with shallow respirations. Distended abdomen with reduced bowel sounds (ileus). No focal neurological deficit, no neck stiffness, no rash. No signs of active infection on exam (no consolidation, no murmur, no cellulitis).
imaging: Chest X-ray: cardiomegaly with possible small pericardial effusion, no consolidation
ECG: sinus bradycardia, low-voltage complexes, prolonged QT interval
microbiology: Blood cultures sent, pending - no clinical evidence of sepsis
differentialDiagnoses: Central nervous system event (stroke) causing coma
finalDiagnosis: Myxoedema coma (decompensated severe primary hypothyroidism) precipitated by cold exposure and thyroid hormone non-adherence
citations: American Thyroid Association Guidelines for Hypothyroidism 2014
contraindications: Avoid rapid rewarming (risk of vasodilation and cardiovascular collapse)
Do not give levothyroxine alone without first addressing possible concurrent adrenal insufficiency - give stress-dose hydrocortisone before/with thyroid hormone replacement
edgeCases: May coexist with adrenal insufficiency (autoimmune polyglandular syndrome) - empiric hydrocortisone should precede or accompany levothyroxine

Hypothermia and bradycardia can mimic or mask concurrent sepsis, which may itself be the precipitant - a low threshold for empiric antibiotics is reasonable if any diagnostic uncertainty exists, pending cultures

Myxoedema coma is not present in the provided diagnosable-disease vocabulary list (closest match 'myxedema' maps to hyperthyroid/thyroid storm category by label but represents the hypothyroid decompensated state here) - mapped to id 'myxedema'
Elevated CK can mimic rhabdomyolysis or ACS workup confounders
Hyponatremia and hypoglycemia can independently alter sensorium, complicating attribution
